events.title: 7 October attacks and the start of bombardment
events.summary: Palestinian armed groups attack communities and military sites in Israel, killing and capturing civilians and soldiers. Israel begins airstrikes on Gaza.
events.context: This is the starting point of the selected chronology, not the beginning of Gaza’s history or the occupation.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Situation overview: attacks, captives and the start of Israeli strikes on 7 October.

events.shortSummary: Palestinian armed groups kill and capture civilians and soldiers in Israel, and Israel begins airstrikes on Gaza.

events.title: Gallant announces a complete siege using dehumanizing language
events.summary: Defence minister Yoav Gallant announces a complete siege: no electricity, food or fuel. In the same announcement he uses the phrase “human animals,” alongside measures cutting off essentials to Gaza’s population.
events.context: The wording is attributed to Gallant’s announcement. The siege restricts necessities on which civilian survival depends.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 9 October announcement: siege measures and quoted dehumanizing language; OCHA Flash Update #4 on essential services.

events.shortSummary: Gallant announces cuts to food, electricity and fuel, using the phrase “human animals” in the same announcement.

events.title: Northern Gaza is ordered to evacuate
events.summary: Israeli forces order roughly 1.1 million people in northern Gaza to move south within 24 hours. OCHA reports mass displacement amid continuing bombardment.
events.context: Displacement does not establish that the places people are directed toward are safe.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Key points: the overnight evacuation order and its 24-hour deadline.

events.shortSummary: Israeli forces order roughly 1.1 million people to leave northern Gaza within 24 hours.

events.title: Ground operations expand as communications go dark
events.summary: A communications blackout cuts contact with Gaza as Israeli ground forces enter more areas. Aid delivery and emergency responders’ ability to locate people are severely disrupted.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.label: 27–28 October 2023
eventTime.rationale: Key points: blackout from 27 October at about 18:00 and ground operations over the following 24 hours.

events.shortSummary: A communications blackout and expanding Israeli ground operations severely disrupt aid and emergency rescue.

events.title: Repeated airstrikes destroy residential blocks in Jabalia
events.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit Jabalia refugee camp on consecutive days. OCHA reports multiple residential buildings destroyed and dozens of people killed.
events.context: The report describes the second strike on 1 November, within 24 hours of the first. The toll is a contemporaneous report, not a final count.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.label: 31 October–1 November 2023
eventTime.rationale: Gaza overview: 1 November strikes on Jabalia residential buildings, the second consecutive day of such strikes.

events.shortSummary: OCHA reports dozens killed and residential buildings destroyed in consecutive Israeli airstrikes on the refugee camp.

events.title: Israeli forces enter Al-Shifa Hospital
events.summary: Israeli troops and tanks enter Gaza’s Al-Shifa Hospital. OCHA reports that almost all northern hospitals with inpatient capacity are no longer admitting patients.
events.context: A later raid in March 2024 is a separate episode. The archive also includes reporting on that later destruction.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Key points: entry into the Shifa compound on 15 November; northern hospital capacity.

events.shortSummary: Israeli troops enter Al-Shifa as OCHA reports almost all northern inpatient hospitals have stopped admitting patients.

events.title: A humanitarian pause begins
events.summary: An agreed pause allows aid deliveries to increase and hostages to be released. The UN scales up deliveries of food, water, fuel and medical supplies.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Flash Update #49, key points: the pause begins at 07:00 on 24 November; first-day aid statement.

events.shortSummary: An agreed pause brings increased food, water and medical deliveries alongside hostage releases.

events.title: South Africa brings a genocide case to the ICJ
events.summary: South Africa files proceedings against Israel under the Genocide Convention concerning Gaza and requests urgent provisional measures.
events.context: Filing a case and the Court’s later interim orders are distinct legal steps.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Opening procedural history: application filed on 29 December 2023.

events.shortSummary: South Africa asks the ICJ for urgent measures under the Genocide Convention.

events.title: The ICJ orders provisional measures
events.summary: The Court orders measures to protect Palestinians in Gaza, prevent acts prohibited by the Genocide Convention, and enable urgently needed humanitarian assistance.
events.context: The order is an interim measure, not a final judgment on the merits of the genocide case.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Conclusion and operative clause: measures adopted on 26 January 2024.

events.shortSummary: The ICJ orders protection measures for Palestinians and urgently needed humanitarian assistance.

events.title: Hind Rajab’s family and the ambulance sent to rescue her are killed
events.summary: PRCS reports that Israeli fire struck the car carrying Hind Rajab and her family and the ambulance dispatched to rescue her. The young girl, her relatives and two paramedics died.
events.context: UN experts record audio accounts of Hind and her cousin pleading for help. The date marks the attack and rescue attempt; it is not a verified time of death for every person.

events.shortSummary: PRCS reports Hind, her relatives and two rescuing paramedics killed after Israeli fire hits their vehicles.

events.title: Israeli raid leaves Nasser Hospital without power or running water
events.summary: Israeli forces enter Nasser Hospital after a siege. WHO later finds the hospital non-functional, without electricity or running water, and reports at least five ICU patients died before rescue missions could reach them.
events.context: 15 February is OCHA’s date for reported entry by Israeli forces; WHO’s later account dates the raid to 14 February. The five reported ICU deaths preceded patient-transfer missions and are not all assigned to 15 February.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Flash Update #119: forces reported inside Nasser on 15 February; WHO account of subsequent patient transfers.

humanImpact.text: WHO transferred 32 critical patients on 18–19 February. Two paralyzed patients needed continuous manual ventilation during transport because portable ventilators were unavailable.
humanImpact.locator: WHO statement: life-saving transfers, patient conditions and lack of portable ventilators.

events.shortSummary: WHO reports Nasser left without power or running water, with at least five ICU patients dead before rescue missions arrived.

events.title: People seeking food are killed on Al Rashid Road
events.summary: More than 100 Palestinians are reported killed as people gather around trucks carrying supplies near Gaza City. OCHA documents the deaths and differing accounts of how they occurred.
events.context: OCHA attributes the initial toll to Gaza’s Ministry of Health and records conflicting initial accounts. The entry does not resolve those accounts into an unsupported finding.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Key highlights and Gaza updates: 29 February aid-truck incident, attributed casualty reports and differing accounts.

events.shortSummary: OCHA reports more than 100 Palestinians killed around food trucks, with conflicting accounts of how they died.

events.title: Children die from malnutrition and dehydration in northern Gaza
events.summary: UNICEF reports that at least ten children have died from dehydration and malnutrition at Kamal Adwan Hospital in recent days. The agency describes these deaths as predictable and preventable.
events.context: This is the statement’s publication date, not a single day on which all the children died. UNICEF calls for food, water and medical supplies to reach children.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 3 March statement: at least ten reported child deaths in recent days; January nutrition screenings in northern Gaza.

humanImpact.text: January screenings in northern Gaza found acute malnutrition in nearly one in six children under two. This describes screened children, not a census of every child in Gaza.
humanImpact.locator: UNICEF statement: January screening results, northern Gaza.

events.shortSummary: UNICEF reports at least ten children dying from malnutrition and dehydration at Kamal Adwan Hospital in recent days.

events.title: Al-Shifa is left in ruins after a two-week Israeli raid
events.summary: Gaza’s largest hospital is left non-functional. WHO’s subsequent visit finds most buildings destroyed or damaged, medical equipment burned and bodies partly buried in the grounds.
events.context: The date marks the withdrawal at the end of the raid. WHO inspected the hospital on 5 April and published its account on 6 April.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: WHO’s 5 April visit: non-functional hospital, destroyed equipment, reported patient deaths and severely damaged buildings.; Humanitarian developments: Israeli forces withdraw on 1 April after a two-week operation at Al-Shifa.

humanImpact.text: WHO found 115 emergency beds burned and 14 neonatal incubators destroyed. The hospital director reported that at least 20 patients died during the siege because care and access were lacking.
humanImpact.locator: WHO statement: emergency department, neonatal equipment and hospital director’s account.

events.shortSummary: WHO finds Gaza’s largest hospital in ruins, with burned medical equipment and bodies in its grounds.

events.title: An Israeli strike kills seven WCK aid workers
events.summary: An Israeli strike hits a World Central Kitchen convoy, killing seven team members. WCK pauses its regional operations.
events.context: The event took place on 1 April; WCK’s statement was published on 2 April. These dates are kept separate.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: WCK response timeline: April 1 convoy strike; 2 April statement: seven deaths and immediate operational pause.

events.shortSummary: An Israeli strike kills seven World Central Kitchen workers and halts WCK’s regional operations.

events.title: Mass graves at hospitals prompt calls for an independent investigation
events.summary: The UN rights office reports hundreds of bodies found at Nasser and Al-Shifa hospitals. It cites accounts of some bodies stripped or with hands bound and calls for independent investigations.
events.context: These are reported discoveries and allegations. The identity of victims and circumstances of their deaths require investigation; the entry does not treat every burial as proof of an execution.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 24 April account of the OHCHR briefing: reported graves at Nasser and Al-Shifa, bodies with bound hands and call for investigation.

events.shortSummary: OHCHR reports hundreds of bodies at hospitals and calls for investigation into accounts of bound and stripped victims.

events.title: The Rafah operation displaces families and closes the crossing
events.summary: Families leave Rafah after evacuation orders. Israeli forces take control of the Gazan side of Rafah Crossing, which closes to goods and people on 7 May.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Rafah developments: evacuation orders on 6 May and closure of the crossing on 7 May.

humanImpact.text: By 29 May, OCHA reported about one million people displaced from Rafah since 6 May. Many were leaving a place where they had already sought refuge. This is cumulative displacement over several weeks.
humanImpact.locator: Key highlights and humanitarian developments: Rafah displacement since 6 May.

events.shortSummary: Israeli evacuation orders displace families, and the closure of Rafah Crossing cuts off movement of goods and people.

events.title: The ICJ issues further measures concerning Rafah
events.summary: The Court issues further measures concerning the Rafah offensive, humanitarian access and access for investigations into allegations of genocide.
events.context: The order requires halting the offensive and other action in Rafah that may impose conditions of life capable of destroying the Palestinian group in Gaza, wholly or partly. It also addresses keeping Rafah Crossing open for urgently needed assistance.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Conclusion and measures: the Rafah order and its conditions.

events.shortSummary: The ICJ orders further measures concerning Rafah, humanitarian access and investigations into genocide allegations.

events.title: An Israeli strike sets displaced families’ tents ablaze in Rafah
events.summary: An airstrike hits a displacement site in northwestern Rafah. Gaza’s Ministry of Health reports 45 people killed and 249 injured; PRCS says people were trapped in burning tents.
events.context: The reported dead include 23 women, children and older people. The Israeli military said it targeted two senior Hamas officials.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Humanitarian developments: evening 26 May strike, PRCS account of people trapped in burning tents, Ministry of Health casualty figures.

events.shortSummary: Gaza’s Ministry of Health reports 45 killed and 249 injured after a strike ignites a Rafah displacement site.

events.title: 274 Palestinians reported killed in the Nuseirat operation
events.summary: OCHA cites Gaza’s Ministry of Health reporting 274 Palestinians killed during an Israeli operation that rescues four hostages. Hospitals are overwhelmed by the mass casualties.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Gaza updates: 8 June Nuseirat operation, hostage rescue and casualties attributed to the Ministry of Health.

events.shortSummary: OCHA cites Gaza’s Ministry of Health reporting 274 Palestinians killed during the operation that rescues four hostages.

events.title: Over 1.9 million people displaced, with basic survival conditions collapsing
events.summary: OCHA reports more than 1.9 million people displaced across Gaza. Families face repeated orders to move, overcrowded shelters and severe shortages of water and sanitation.
events.context: The date marks publication of a snapshot of cumulative displacement and living conditions, not a single mass movement on that day.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 12 July update: more than 1.9 million displaced; UNRWA’s Deir al-Balah shelter account and WASH water-availability estimates.

humanImpact.text: At one Deir al-Balah school shelter, UNRWA reported about 14,000 people sharing 25 toilets. This example describes that shelter, not every displacement site.
humanImpact.locator: UNRWA account of conditions at the Deir al-Balah school shelter.

events.shortSummary: OCHA reports more than 1.9 million displaced people facing overcrowded shelters and severe water and sanitation shortages.

events.title: 90 reported killed in strikes on Al-Mawasi’s “humanitarian zone”
events.summary: Israeli strikes hit displacement tents, a food kitchen and a water point in an area Israel had designated a humanitarian zone. Gaza’s Ministry of Health reports 90 people killed and 300 injured.
events.context: OCHA reports that Nasser Hospital was overwhelmed, with patients treated on the floor and shortages of medical supplies. The initial toll remains attributed to the Ministry of Health.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Humanitarian developments: 13 July strikes on tents, a food kitchen and a water point; Ministry of Health toll and overwhelmed Nasser Hospital.

events.shortSummary: Gaza’s Ministry of Health reports 90 killed and 300 injured in strikes on an Israel-designated humanitarian zone.

events.title: UN report documents torture and humiliation of Palestinian detainees
events.summary: OHCHR describes thousands of Palestinians detained, often without charges or trial. Testimonies describe beatings, electric shocks, forced nudity and sexual violence, including rape, in Israeli custody.
events.context: The report covers October 2023–June 2024 and includes detainees from Gaza and the West Bank. These findings and testimonies are attributed to OHCHR; individual allegations are not recast as criminal convictions.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 31 July report covering October 2023–June 2024: arbitrary detention, torture testimonies, sexual violence and at least 53 deaths in Israeli custody.

humanImpact.text: OHCHR reported at least 53 Palestinian deaths in Israeli detention facilities and prisons since 7 October 2023. This includes people from Gaza and the West Bank; the figure does not establish the cause of every death.
humanImpact.locator: Report release: deaths in detention, geographical scope and assessment period.

events.shortSummary: OHCHR records accounts of beatings, electric shocks, forced nudity and sexual violence in Israeli custody.

events.title: A strike on Al-Tabi’een school kills people sheltering and praying
events.summary: An Israeli strike hits the school’s prayer hall during dawn prayers, where displaced families are sheltering. Palestinian Civil Defense initially reports about 90 killed, including children and women.
events.context: This is an initial reported toll. OCHA situates the attack within a repeated pattern of strikes on schools used as shelters.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Humanitarian developments: 10 August strike during dawn prayers; Civil Defense initial toll and OHCHR school-shelter strike series since 4 July.

humanImpact.text: By 12 August, OHCHR had recorded 21 strikes on schools serving as shelters since 4 July, with at least 274 reported deaths. That figure covers multiple attacks, not only Al-Tabi’een.
humanImpact.locator: OHCHR account of the school-shelter strike series.

events.shortSummary: Palestinian Civil Defense initially reports about 90 killed in a strike during dawn prayers at a school shelter.

events.title: An emergency polio vaccination campaign begins
events.summary: Following Gaza’s first reported polio case in 25 years, health teams begin an emergency campaign to vaccinate children. Humanitarian pauses allow the initial phase to proceed.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Opening and campaign overview: start on 1 September; first phase on 1–3 September.

events.shortSummary: Health teams begin emergency vaccinations after Gaza’s first reported polio case in 25 years.

events.title: A renewed siege tightens around northern Gaza
events.summary: Jabalya, Beit Hanoun and Beit Lahiya come under an intensified Israeli siege. OCHA records widespread denial and obstruction of humanitarian access.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.label: Early October 2024
eventTime.rationale: October access snapshot: siege since approximately 6 October and the denial of North Gaza missions.

events.shortSummary: OCHA reports an intensified siege of northern towns and widespread obstruction of humanitarian access.

events.title: The ICC issues warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant
events.summary: The International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant concerning alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.
events.context: Arrest warrants are not criminal convictions. This entry records the warrants’ issuance on this date, not their current procedural status.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 21 November press release: warrants and reasonable-grounds findings.

events.shortSummary: The ICC issues warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant concerning alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.

events.title: An Israeli raid shuts North Gaza’s last major hospital
events.summary: WHO reports that a raid puts Kamal Adwan Hospital out of service, with key departments burned. Patients and staff are forced to leave; initial reports describe people being stripped and made to walk south.
events.context: WHO says the hospital’s director was reportedly detained. The accounts of stripping and forced movement are identified as initial reports, not direct observations by WHO.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 28 December statement: previous day’s raid, hospital closure, transferred patients and initial accounts of forced stripping and movement south.

humanImpact.text: WHO reported 15 critical patients transferred to the damaged Indonesian Hospital, which lacked equipment and supplies to provide adequate care. The raid removed North Gaza’s last major functioning health facility.
humanImpact.locator: WHO statement: critical patient transfers and remaining hospital capacity.

events.shortSummary: WHO reports North Gaza’s last major hospital shut by an Israeli raid, with initial accounts of forced stripping and evacuation.

events.title: A ceasefire takes effect
events.summary: A ceasefire begins in Gaza, with an initial 42-day phase. Aid deliveries increase as hostages and Palestinian detainees begin to be released under the agreement.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Key highlights and humanitarian developments: ceasefire effective at 11:15 on 19 January; terms of the first phase.

events.shortSummary: A ceasefire increases aid deliveries and begins releases of hostages and Palestinian detainees.

events.title: UN commission finds destruction of reproductive healthcare and genocidal acts
events.summary: A UN commission finds that attacks on maternity and reproductive facilities, and restrictions on medical supplies, devastate pregnancy and childbirth care. It concludes that preventing births and imposing destructive conditions amount to genocidal acts.
events.context: The findings are those of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry, not a final court judgment. This entry uses March 2025 because institutional release metadata differs between 12 and 13 March.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.label: March 2025
eventTime.rationale: March 2025 report: destruction of reproductive healthcare and birth-prevention findings. UN reproduction metadata and release indexes differ by one day (12/13 March); month precision retained.

events.shortSummary: A UN commission finds reproductive healthcare devastated and concludes that birth-prevention measures and destructive conditions amount to genocidal acts.

events.title: Israel blocks the entry of aid and supplies
events.summary: Israeli authorities stop the entry of humanitarian aid and other supplies into Gaza. The closure interrupts food, medicine and fuel deliveries.

review.method: Date and summary cross-checked against cited primary-source text; no human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: Response update: closure since 2 March; 18 March briefing: entry of lifesaving supplies cut off from that date.

events.shortSummary: Israel stops humanitarian aid and other supplies from entering Gaza, interrupting food, medicine and fuel deliveries.

events.title: Large-scale Israeli airstrikes resume
events.summary: Intense Israeli airstrikes resume in Gaza. The UN relief chief reports the renewed bombardment alongside the continuing cutoff of lifesaving supplies.

eventTime.rationale: 18 March Security Council briefing: renewed intense airstrikes and the continuing supply cutoff.

events.shortSummary: Intense Israeli airstrikes resume while lifesaving supplies remain cut off.

events.title: 15 Palestinian rescue workers are killed; bodies and vehicles buried
events.summary: OCHA reports emergency crews struck one after another while searching for missing colleagues in Rafah. Available information points to Israeli forces; 15 responders’ bodies are found buried with wrecked emergency vehicles.
events.context: The dead include eight PRCS workers, six Civil Defense members and one UNRWA worker. Most bodies were recovered on 30 March, after responders went missing on 23 March. Five clearly marked ambulances, a fire truck and a UN car were buried with them.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

events.shortSummary: OCHA reports 15 responders found buried with emergency vehicles after crews were struck while searching for colleagues.

events.title: Militarized food-distribution sites open amid UN warnings
events.summary: The Gaza Humanitarian Foundation begins operating distribution sites. The UN refuses to participate and warns that the scheme violates humanitarian principles and puts people seeking food at risk.
events.context: The UN’s assessment is attributed to the UN. A later entry documents deaths near distribution sites and along food-convoy routes, with those locations counted separately.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

events.title: More than 1,300 Palestinians reported killed while seeking food
events.summary: OHCHR reports at least 1,373 Palestinians killed while seeking food between 27 May and 31 July. It attributes most killings to the Israeli military and says it has no information that the victims posed a threat or were participating in hostilities.
events.context: The date is OCHA’s publication date for this account of OHCHR’s 31 July findings. It describes repeated killings over two months, not a single incident.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 6 August update, Impact of Military Activity: OHCHR’s 31 July account of 1,373 deaths seeking food between 27 May and 31 July; separate location totals and attribution.

humanImpact.text: Of those deaths, 859 were near militarized distribution sites and 514 along humanitarian food-convoy routes. The total is not a count solely of deaths at Gaza Humanitarian Foundation sites.
humanImpact.locator: OHCHR’s separate distribution-site and convoy-route counts, cited by OCHA.

events.shortSummary: OHCHR reports at least 1,373 Palestinians killed seeking food between 27 May and 31 July, mostly by the Israeli military.

events.title: Famine is formally confirmed in Gaza Governorate
events.summary: An IPC assessment confirms famine in Gaza Governorate. UN agencies describe widespread starvation and preventable deaths, with more than half a million people trapped in famine.
events.context: 22 August is the announcement date; the assessment confirms famine in Gaza Governorate as of 15 August. This is not a blanket classification of every area in the Gaza Strip.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

humanImpact.text: UN agencies report more than 12,000 children identified with acute malnutrition in July, nearly a quarter with its severe form. This is the July figure, not an August or present-day total.
humanImpact.locator: Joint agency release: July child malnutrition figures and severity.

events.shortSummary: UN agencies describe more than half a million people trapped in famine, with widespread starvation and preventable deaths.

events.title: UN commission finds Israel committed genocide in Gaza
events.summary: The Independent International Commission of Inquiry concludes that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. It finds killings, serious bodily or mental harm, destructive conditions of life and measures intended to prevent births.
events.context: The commission assesses intent through official statements and the pattern of conduct. This is an investigative commission’s finding; the ICJ’s provisional orders are separately documented and are not a final genocide judgment.

review.method: Dates, attributed figures and summaries checked against cited original-source text. Where direct retrieval was blocked, indexed text from the institutional original was consulted; no independent verification or human editorial approval claimed.

eventTime.rationale: 16 September release: commission finds four categories of genocidal acts, assessing conduct and statements for intent; distinct from an ICJ judgment.

events.shortSummary: The UN commission concludes Israel committed genocide through killings, serious harm, destructive living conditions and measures intended to prevent births.

events.title: Another ceasefire takes effect

curation.method: AI-assisted source check emphasizing attacks on civilians and documented patterns of deprivation, displacement, dehumanization and abuse. Direct report text was used where accessible; some blocked institutional originals were consulted through indexed text, recorded on each reference. Selected coverage, not independent verification of every allegation.
curation.archiveLinks: Manually selected related reading, not evidence of event time unless included in sourceIds.
curation.selection: Include mass civilian harm and treatment of Palestinians alongside major military, aid and legal developments. No ranking of victims or atrocities. Report findings use publication dates, distinct from the period of abuse.
curation.datePolicy: Incident dates, report publication dates, assessment dates and uncertain dates are explicitly separated. Month-precision findings do not claim a particular day.
